# Task Card Rules Checklist: Taskify Kanban Board

**Purpose**: Validate the requirements quality of task status-change, assignment, and
comment rules — the recently clarified permission logic (FR-007, FR-008, FR-009,
FR-013, FR-014) — ahead of `/speckit-tasks`.
**Created**: 2026-10-29
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is a maximum length or character constraint specified for task title and description? [Gap, Spec §FR-006]
- [x] CHK002 Is a maximum length or character constraint specified for comment text? [Gap, Spec §FR-013]
- [x] CHK003 Does a requirement address project-name uniqueness, or is duplication explicitly allowed? [Gap, Spec §FR-004]
- [x] CHK004 Is there a requirement covering assignment to an invalid/unknown user identifier? [Gap, Spec §FR-007]
- [x] CHK005 Is there a requirement defining whether an "edited" indicator is shown on a comment after FR-014 applies? [Gap, Spec §FR-014]
- [x] CHK006 Is there a requirement on what feedback a blocked move (FR-008) surfaces to the non-assignee who attempted it, beyond "prevent the move"? [Gap, Spec Edge Cases]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK007 Is "whitespace-only" comment text explicitly classified as empty, or left to interpretation of FR-013's "empty-text" wording? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-013]
- [x] CHK008 Is the Product Manager vs. Engineer role distinction clarified as identification-only with zero functional/permission effect, anywhere a reader would look first (e.g., Key Entities)? [Clarity, Spec §Key Entities]
- [x] CHK009 Is it clear whether the move-permission check (FR-008) is evaluated at the moment of the move request against the task's current assignee, rather than against some cached/earlier assignee value? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK010 Does the Assumptions statement that "all five users have equal capabilities" (no role-based permission differences) still read as accurate now that FR-008/FR-014 impose assignee-based and author-based restrictions, or does it need a qualifying note distinguishing role-based from assignment-based restriction? [Conflict, Spec §Assumptions vs §Clarifications]
- [x] CHK011 Is column/status terminology used consistently (e.g., always "column") across User Stories, Edge Cases, and Functional Requirements, without drifting to synonyms like "state" or "stage"? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK012 Are the FR-007 (assignment, unrestricted) and FR-008 (move, assignee-restricted) requirements cross-referenced so a reader understands why assignment is open while movement is not? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, §FR-008]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK013 Can User Story 1's blocked-move acceptance scenario be objectively verified without implementation detail (e.g., is "the system MUST prevent the move" measurable as pass/fail)? [Measurability, Spec §User Story 1 Scenario 3]
- [x] CHK014 Does Success Criteria define a measurable outcome for the blocked-move path (non-assignee attempt), or only for the successful-move path (SC-003)? [Gap, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [x] CHK015 Is "immediately" in User Story 3's comment-edit acceptance scenario given any bound, or left as an unquantified term distinct from SC-006's "no page reload required"? [Clarity, Spec §User Story 3]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK016 Is a requirement defined for near-simultaneous reassignment of the same task by two different users to two different people (reassignment race), beyond the general "last update applied" rule for moves? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [x] CHK017 Is a requirement defined for the sequence "task reassigned to User B while User A's move request is in flight" — does the newly reassigned user's permission take effect before, during, or after A's pending request resolves? [Edge Case, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007, §FR-008]
- [x] CHK018 Are requirements defined for a comment-edit or comment-delete attempted on a task whose assignee has since changed (verifying author-based comment permission is independent of task assignment)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-014]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK019 Is the dependency between FR-008's "unassigned tasks movable by any user" rule and FR-007's "any user can assign/unassign" rule documented as a deliberate pairing (to avoid lockout), or does a reader have to infer it from the Edge Cases note alone? [Traceability, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK020 Is the assumption that no concurrency-control mechanism (e.g., optimistic locking) is needed for the permission checks in FR-008/FR-014 explicitly stated, or only implied by the "last update wins" edge case? [Assumption, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK021 Is there any remaining ambiguity between "any of the five users" (FR-004, FR-007) and "only the task's current assignee" (FR-008) regarding who counts as an eligible actor for each action? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004, §FR-007, §FR-008]
- [x] CHK022 Do the Clarifications session bullets and their corresponding Functional Requirements state the same rule without contradiction (spot-check each of the three 2026-10-29 entries against FR-007/FR-008/FR-014)? [Conflict, Spec §Clarifications]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
